title: One vendor-agnostic client is the sole reader of secret material
iWant: a single named module every call site imports to read secrets
soThat: changing vendors is a one-module change and duplicate read paths cannot drift

acceptanceCriteria.description: The project exposes one Secrets Manager module whose public surface is `get(name)`, `getRequired(name)`, `list()`, and `refresh()`; the module is the only importer of the vendor binding on the boundary.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project that has applied the blueprint and realised TAC-901
acceptanceCriteria.when: the source tree is scanned for imports of the vendor SDK identifier or of any additional secrets-reader module
acceptanceCriteria.then: the only source file that imports the vendor SDK is the Secrets Manager module and no other module names an alternative secrets-reader import

acceptanceCriteria.description: `getRequired(name)` on an absent required secret throws a stable-coded error naming the logical name and the active environment.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a manifest entry `X` marked `required: true` with no resolvable per-environment path in the active environment
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call throws a `SECRETS_REQUIRED_ABSENT` error whose message names `X` and the active environment string, and no secret value is served

acceptanceCriteria.description: `refresh()` re-reads exactly the declared slice from the vendor and updates the in-memory cache atomically; a caller invoking `get` mid-refresh sees either the previous full slice or the new full slice, never a mix.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running process holding a cached slice
acceptanceCriteria.when: a `refresh()` call runs while a concurrent `get(name)` call is in flight
acceptanceCriteria.then: the concurrent `get(name)` returns either the pre-refresh value or the post-refresh value; it never returns null when both refresh states have a value, and it never returns a mixed-slice combination across two names
